description: Let signed-in users set a listing aside: a heart button on every listing card and a My favorites page. Each favorite keeps a snapshot of the listing's display fields and stays readable after the listing expires or is deleted. Out of scope: notifications, folders, sharing, anonymous favorites.

userStories.title: API contract for favorites
userStories.description: As a developer, I change the OpenAPI contract first (the project is contract-first) to expose the favorites endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: openapi/favorite-api.yaml declares POST /api/favorites, DELETE /api/favorites/{listingId}, GET /api/favorites (paginated) and GET /api/favorites/ids
POST answers 201, 401, 404, 409 (already a favorite), 422
/api/favorites/ids is declared before /api/favorites/{listingId}
The build generates the FavoriteApi interface; generated code is never edited
Build passes

userStories.title: Favorite model, snapshot and repository
userStories.description: As a developer, I store a favorite with a snapshot of the listing's display fields.
acceptanceCriteria: Favorite holds userId, listingId, createdAt and an embedded ListingSnapshot
Uniqueness of (userId, listingId) is checked in the service, not only by an index
Repository tests pass

userStories.title: Create and delete a favorite
userStories.description: As a signed-in user, I add or remove a favorite.
acceptanceCriteria: Adding an existing favorite returns 409 with an RFC 7807 problem body
Adding a favorite on an unknown listing returns 404
Deleting is idempotent from the user's point of view
Unit tests cover the three cases; all tests pass

userStories.title: List favorites with fallback on the snapshot
userStories.description: As a signed-in user, I see my favorites, even those whose listing is gone.
acceptanceCriteria: Each item exposes sourceAvailable and expired
When the listing still exists, the snapshot is refreshed on read
When it does not, the snapshot is returned, read-only
All tests pass

userStories.title: Heart button on listing cards
userStories.description: As a signed-in user, I toggle a favorite from a listing card.
acceptanceCriteria: The button is hidden for anonymous visitors
Clicking it does not follow the card link (stopPropagation + preventDefault)
The state comes from a single call to /api/favorites/ids
Component tests pass
Verify in browser

userStories.title: My favorites page
userStories.description: As a signed-in user, I browse my favorites in my account area.
acceptanceCriteria: Paginated list, newest first
Expired and No longer available badges; no contact button on those items
Empty state with a link back to the listings
Component tests pass
Verify in browser
